decisive_items: a 17 × 9 cm mixed solid and cystic mass occupying the right hepatic lobe with compression of the inferior vena cava (IVC)
an infrarenal IVC thrombus and a near-occlusive embolus in the left pulmonary artery
persistent sanguineous output from the drain led to anemia and concern for hemorrhage
response.rationale: The vignette describes a young child with a large hepatic mass, vascular invasion (IVC thrombus, pulmonary embolus), and hemorrhagic complications, most consistent with hepatoblastoma. R4 (undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma) is a less common pediatric hepatic malignancy but can present similarly; however, hepatoblastoma is more typical in this age group. Benign lesions (R1/R3/R5/R7) and abscess (R6) are contradicted by vascular invasion and hemorrhage. R9/R8/R11/R10 are complications rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Less common than hepatoblastoma in an 8-year-old; no specific distinguishing features provided.
Benign vascular tumor; contradicted by hemorrhage and vascular invasion.
Adenoma rare in children and contradicted by hemorrhage/invasion.
FNH is benign and does not cause vascular invasion or hemorrhage.
Abscess would show infection signs and not a solid-cystic mass with vascular invasion.
IVC thrombosis is a complication of the mass, not the primary diagnosis.
Thrombosis is a complication, not the underlying cause.
Abdominal compartment syndrome is a consequence, not the diagnosis.
Pulmonary embolism is a complication of the tumor thrombus.
